# PEN-2585 — point `AGENT_HOME` at a path the pod actually mounts

PR: _(filed from PEN-2585; see the issue for the measurement trail)_

## Files

- `src/server/job-manifest.ts`
- `src/server/job-manifest.agent-home.test.ts` (new)

## What changed

`buildEnvVars` previously projected `AGENT_HOME` straight from
`workspaceContext.agentHome`. The server computes that as
`resolveDefaultAgentWorkspaceDir(agent.id)` = `<instanceRoot>/workspaces/<agentId>`
and `mkdir -p`s it on **its own** `/paperclip` mount before handing it over.

The pod mounts no such path. Measured 2026-11-07 on the live Cto pod
(`claude_k8s`, external instructions bundle):

```
the exported agent-home path   ->  <instanceRoot>/workspaces/<agentId>  ->  ENOENT
ls /paperclip/instances/default                                         ->  data  skills
findmnt -T /paperclip/instances/default                                 ->  emptyDir instance-overlay
```

`instances/default` arrives as the 16 MiB `instance-overlay` emptyDir with `data/`
and `skills/` bound over it and **nothing** bound at `workspaces/`. So the variable
was set, pointed at an identically-spelled directory on a volume the pod does not
have, and every `$AGENT_HOME/...` read was ENOENT.

This is PEN-4932 invariant 9 — the failure `isWorkspaceLessFallbackWorkspaceDir`
already documents for the workspace cwd ("the server realizes every execution
workspace onto its OWN `/paperclip` mount … the pod's identically-spelled path
resolves to nothing") — reached through a second variable that nothing guards.

Now `AGENT_HOME` resolves through **`agentBundleRoot`** — the same helper
`resolveScopedWritableMounts` derives the writable instructions mount from, fed the
same input (`config.instructionsFilePath`, which that resolver receives as
`agentInstructionsFilePath`) — gated on the same on-volume test its `accept()` applies.
So the variable names a mounted path *by construction* rather than by coincidence:
the per-seat CephFS directory on the `paperclip-data` PVC, which is also where the
charter's companions live, so `$AGENT_HOME/{HEARTBEAT,SOUL,TOOLS}.md` resolve for the
first time. Agents with no bundle on the volume keep the previous value unchanged.

**The fix is a join, not a value.** The original defect was an env var with no
relation to any mount, so a fix that produces the right *string* by a second route is
the same shape of mistake. The file already states that discipline fifty lines below
`agentBundleRoot`, for the read-only withdrawal: *"two derivations of this path could
disagree, and the permissive direction of that disagreement is the rw mount this
exists to withdraw."* The permissive direction here is an `AGENT_HOME` naming a tree
the pod never mounted.

### The spelling this entry originally shipped, and why it was wrong

The first cut keyed on `instructionsBundleMode === "external"` + `instructionsRootPath`.
That is exactly such a second derivation, and the two **agree only for `external`**.
`agent-instructions.ts` persists `instructionsRootPath = dirname(instructionsFilePath)`
(`syncInstructionsBundleConfigFromFilePath`), so:

| mode | `instructionsRootPath` | `agentBundleRoot(instructionsFilePath)` |
|---|---|---|
| `external` | `…/agents/<slug>` | `…/agents/<slug>` — same |
| `managed` | `…/agents/<id>/`**`instructions`** | `…/agents/<id>` — **differ by one level** |

`managed` is not hypothetical: it is one of only two modes the service can persist
(`type BundleMode = "managed" | "external"`), and one live `claude_k8s` seat is on it.
That branch therefore missed `managed` seats entirely — and extending it to
`|| "managed"` would have been worse than leaving it: the seat would get an
`AGENT_HOME` that is durable and mounted but **one level too deep**, putting
`$AGENT_HOME/memory/` *inside* the instructions bundle rather than beside it, which is
not where the candidate list's own comment puts it (*"open the whole agent dir so
`memory/` is covered too"*). Not broken — silently the wrong directory, forever.

Caught in review by @Ceo before merge (PEN-2585, 2026-11-07T02:1xZ), from the source
rather than from the PR description. Keying on `agentBundleRoot` is strictly smaller
than `external || managed`: one derivation, no mode test at all.

### The on-volume test is not redundant

`agentBundleRoot` refuses only the volume *root*; it does not test that the path is on
the volume at all. `resolveScopedWritableMounts` applies that test separately, in
`accept()`, and creates the mount iff it passes. So an operator-set bundle outside the
data mount — the case `warnIfPersistentTreeIsOffVolume` exists for — would otherwise
produce a durable-**looking** `AGENT_HOME` that no mount backs: PEN-2585 again, by a
new route. Gating on the same predicate makes "mounted" and "exported" the same
condition.

This is the fix `opencode_k8s` shipped at its own copy of this call site. Note its
comment there asserts *"claude_k8s agents (whose AGENT_HOME already IS the bundle
dir) worked"* — that premise is **false** and was never measured against this tree,
which is why the bug outlived the change that named it. The sibling comment is left
alone here; this entry is the correction of record.

The `AGENT_HOME` row in the env-classification table also claimed the value was
"on the mounted PVC" unqualified. True when a bundle is on the volume, false for the
fallback; the reason string now says which is which. Classification is unchanged
(`SAFE_LITERAL` — a filesystem path either way, never credential material).

## Why a manifest test

`job-manifest.agent-home.test.ts` asserts the env value **and** that a volumeMount
with that exact `mountPath` exists on the container that reads it. The half that was
missing all along is the join: an env var naming a durable-looking path proves nothing
on its own, which is exactly what shipped.

The suite asserts that join in **both** modes, which is the point. Against the
`instructionsRootPath` spelling the assertion is *vacuous* for `external` — the two
derivations coincide there, so it cannot fail — and it is the assertion that fails for
`managed`. A suite that exercises only the mode where a defect has no effect reports
green on the defect; that is how the first cut passed 5 of 5.

Controls, both run rather than reasoned about:

- against **`master`** (no `AGENT_HOME` branch at all): **5 of 8 fail**;
- against **the first cut** (`instructionsRootPath` spelling): **4 of 8 fail** — all
  three `managed` cases, plus the off-volume control.

Two fixtures from the first cut were removed as **unreachable config**, not merely
redundant: they pinned `instructionsFilePath` while clearing the mode or the root out
from under it. `syncInstructionsBundleConfigFromFilePath` deletes the mode, root and
entry keys together whenever `instructionsFilePath` is absent, and derives all three
whenever it is present — so "no bundle" is all four fields unset at once, and a bundle
file with a cleared mode cannot be persisted. They encoded the old branch's two falsy
legs rather than any shape the server can produce. Replaced by the real legacy shape
and by an off-volume bundle; the negative control pinning the old server-side path as
mounted nowhere is unchanged.

## Blast radius

Env-only, one adapter, one variable. No manifest shape, mount set, PATH or
credential wiring changes — `AGENT_HOME` is *read* from the mount set, never added to
it, so no seat gains access to anything it did not already mount. Agents with no
instructions bundle on the data mount are byte-identical. Relative to the first cut,
the behaviour change is confined to `managed` seats (previously the broken fallback,
now the agent dir) and to off-volume bundles (now the fallback instead of an unmounted
path).
